text: oh that worked fucking beautifully. like a hot knife to butter. alright lets get those vertex dots and edge selections in next :D
resolution: Vertex dots + edge-highlight overlay + the native marquee rectangle (deferred from the input-loop slice). All three are drawn as screen-space capsules projected with the EXACT render camera, so each dot/line sits on the pixel its raycast shoots back through — pixel-locked at any zoom, the property the old JS overlay lacked. Capsules ride the existing 2D draw-command z-order, so emitting them right after the Scene3D composite (engine.zig drawEditorOverlay call) lands them on top with no new pipeline and no depth fight (draw-on-top is the Blockbench edit-mode convention). Vertex mode draws every vertex as a dot (selected orange+bigger, capped at 80k beyond which only selected draw — fps guard, wireframe still shows topology); edge mode highlights selected edges as orange lines over the wireframe; the marquee box outline now draws live during a left drag-select. The emit lives in 3d.zig because it needs the GPU/capsule module; mesh_edit stays GPU-free with plain read accessors (vertPosPub/vertSelectedPub/edgeEndpointsPub/edgeSelectedPub/ensureTopologyPub) so its topology+selection logic remains unit-testable without wgpu — that split is why test-mesh-edit still passes after the refactor. Built clean; headless RJIT_MESHMODE=1 shows dots at every vertex. Live feel verifies in rjit dev.
